name: Gienah
description: A giant of type B8 III 47.1 parsecs away, 3.8 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Narrabri intensity interferometer.

paper.credit: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417

radius.source: Computed here, not printed by a paper: 3.8 +/- 0.31 solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.75 +/- 0.06 mas of Hanbury Brown, Davis & Allen (1974), MNRAS 167, 121 (the Narrabri intensity interferometer; Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, Table 1, and the JMDC) and the Hipparcos parallax 21.23 +/- 0.2 mas (van Leeuwen 2007, XHIP)

temperature.source: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 106625: effective temperature 12450 +/- 530 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331, XHIP, HIP 59803: RV -4.2 +/- 2.6 km/s (quality A)

distance.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 59803: the Hipparcos parallax (van Leeuwen 2007) the radius is computed with, 21.23 +/- 0.2 mas, inverted

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: A giant of type B8 III, 47 parsecs away: 3.8 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 0.75 milliarcseconds, which at its distance is 3.8 solar radii, and its surface is at 12,450 K.
text.locator: Tables 1 and 6, HD 106625: MK type, limb-darkened diameter, effective temperature
